**Finding submitted: deviation (fallback-level cure).**

- **Responsive clause:** § 4 Term and Termination, ¶ p0016 (the only termination machinery; ¶¶ p0019–p0022 cover post-termination effects, with no refund or early-termination fee mechanics elsewhere).
- **What passes fallback:** AP's for-any-reason exit on 90 days' notice after the 1-year Initial Term sits inside the 60–90 day band, and the only consideration on exit is "fees generated during the termination period" — i.e. capped at the 90-day notice period, no more than three months of fees.
- **What failed:** the same sentence let Kubient terminate for any reason at any point after the Initial Term. Because the effective date was not tied to the end of the then-current renewal term, auto-renewal alone did not make Kubient's right term-end-only, so Kubient could walk away mid-term.
- **Cure (single surgical replace):** AP's 90-day right retained; Kubient's for-any-reason termination is now effective only at the end of the then-current Term, on the same 90 days' notice. All untouched words — including the Initial Term lock-up and the fees-during-termination-period sentence — are preserved verbatim.
- **Not pursued:** the preferred 30-day/pro-rata refund position (no prepaid fees under this auction revenue model) and the mutual Initial Term lock-up (a 12-month term is not a deviation under the detection guidance) — both noted in the rationale rather than redlined.
